hook: A Category 5 hurricane with 180 mph winds, seen from space.
narration: This is a Category 5 hurricane, with sustained winds of one hundred eighty miles an hour.
Hurricane Dorian, filmed from the International Space Station on September 1, 2019.
The station was two hundred sixty miles up.
Below, Dorian was churning over the northern Bahamas.
The dark dot in the middle is the eye. It is calm inside, but the ring of cloud around it holds the storm's worst winds.
It carried the strongest winds in recorded history for the northwestern Bahamas.
outcome: That day, Dorian brought catastrophic damage to the Abacos and Grand Bahama Island.
title: Category 5 Hurricane Dorian from space
question_comment: Would you stay or evacuate for a Category 5 storm?

facts.claim: ISS cameras captured Dorian Sept 1 from 260 miles over the northern Bahamas
facts.source_quote: Cameras outside the International Space Station captured views September 1 of Hurricane Dorian from 260 miles in altitude at 12:16 p.m. Eastern time as it churned over the Atlantic Ocean over the northern Bahamas.
